(D) CORRECTS THE ROUTER'S COMPOUND-CORNER NUMBER. The router quoted 0.95 pF for '6.1 pF lumped + R = 52.5 + the low-L end of the band'. At the LOW-L end (18.5 nH) the exact null needs 0.5915 pF, not 0.95 - it misses the 1 pF stop by 0.4085 pF, nearly half a picofarad, not a graze. The 0.95 pF figure belongs to the CENTRAL residual, 19.5 nH (see nd_r525_p61_l195). The conclusion is unchanged and the direction is the same; the magnitude was understated.
(D) where the router's 0.95 pF actually belongs: 6.1 pF lump, R = 52.5, CENTRAL L = 19.5 nH -> 0.9508 pF. That one really is a graze - 0.049 pF below the stop.

(D) THE PRICE OF BOTTOMING OUT AT THE COMPOUND WORST CORNER, measured as (perfect null) minus (clamped at the 1 pF stop) at 6.1 pF / R 52.5 / 18.5 nH: 0.0175 dB. Missing the null by 0.41 pF costs under two hundredths of a decibel, because at R = 52.5 the reflection is already dominated by Reff = 52.661 ohm and the residual susceptance error is a second-order term on top of it. RL there is 31.710 dB - still 5.7 dB clear of crit. 2.
(D) same at the central 19.5 nH, where the miss is only 0.049 pF: 0.0003 dB. Unmeasurable.
(D) crit. 2 still holds at the compound worst corner with C1 bottomed out: 31.710 dB.
(D) the same number as a tripwire window.

(D) the DEEPEST clamp anywhere in the sweep - 6.5 pF (past the conservative convention), R 52.5, 18.5 nH, where the null wants 0.1915 pF and gets 1 pF, a 0.81 pF miss: 31.660 dB. Even there the penalty is 0.068 dB.

(D) the LARGEST clamp penalty anywhere in the 48-build grid is not at the binding corner at all - it is 0.354 dB at R = 50 / 6.5 pF / 18.5 nH, where RL is 55.108 dB instead of 55.462 dB. A dB penalty near a deep null is arithmetically large and physically irrelevant: both are 30 dB inside spec.

(B) SIMULATED PROOF THAT THE NOMINAL SETTING IS A REAL NULL: with a 1 A AC probe, Im{Zin} = 0 ohm at R = 50 / 5.4 pF / 19.5 nH. The pre-re-route board could not produce this - its trimmer was clamped and Im{Zin} was nonzero by construction.
(B) and what is left after the null: Re{Zin} = Reff = R + X^2/R = 50 + 3.0631^2/50 = 50.1876 ohm. That residual 50.19 ohm IS the 54.55 dB the nominal build reads.
(B) the worst build is a real null too: Im{Zin} = 0 at R = 52.5 / 4.7 pF / 23.3 nH.
(B) Re{Zin} = 52.755 ohm there = 52.5 + 3.66^2/52.5. The whole 31.43 dB worst case is a pure resistance error; no setting of a shunt capacitor can improve it (reff_limit.cir proves why).

(B) THE CONTRAST that makes the two probes above mean something. At the compound worst corner (6.1 pF lump, R 52.5, 18.5 nH) C1 IS clamped, so Im{Zin} is NOT nulled - it measures -0.1779 ohm. The sign says which way: the null wants 6.6915 pF of TOTAL shunt C and the stop forces 7.1 pF, so the port is OVER-corrected and the residual susceptance is capacitive, i.e. Im{Zin} < 0. A reading of zero here would mean the bench had stopped clamping and the honest edge had been simulated away.

(C) TWO-SIDEDNESS DEMONSTRATED at the tightest corner that has it - R = 52.5, 5.4 pF, 18.5 nH, null at 1.2915 pF with only 0.2915 pF of downward room. Moving C1 DOWN by that whole step, to the 1 pF stop, is worse than the null by 0.00890 dB, so the null is genuinely bracketed from below by a reachable setting. The penalty is tiny because at R = 52.5 the reflection is already Reff-dominated - which is the same reason the compound worst corner costs so little when it does bottom out.

(C) and moving the same 0.2915 pF step UP (to 1.5830 pF) is worse by 0.00890 dB. Symmetric to five decimals, which is what a true interior minimum of |Gamma| looks like. Both neighbours are inside the delivered 1-30 pF range.
(C) the null setting at that corner: 1.2915 pF.

(C) the same three-point test at the NOMINAL build (R = 50, 5.4 pF, 19.5 nH, null at 2.3708 pF): going down the full 1.3708 pF of downward authority, to the 1 pF stop, costs 9.681 dB. That 9.7 dB IS the value of the re-route at nominal resistance - it is what the pre-re-route board was paying, involuntarily, every build.
(C) and the same 1.3708 pF step up (to 3.7416 pF) costs 9.681 dB. Both settings are orderable; the null is interior and symmetric.
(C) the nominal null setting, cross-checked against s11_band.cir ct_nom_pf: 2.3708 pF.
(C) RL at that null, cross-checking s11_band.cir rl_r50_p54_l195_fc to 4 decimals: 54.549 dB. Three independent instantiations of the same operating point across two benches.
